a1: Trips, from odometer and the parked/driving state
a2: Charges: measured when seen live, inferred and marked ≈ otherwise
a3: Parked loss, capacity estimate, projected range
a6: A data-quality card with safe fixes
also: Also: units in km or miles, a theme that follows the system, redacted diagnostics, a raw-data viewer, demo mode with a fictional Enyaq, and fifteen languages: Catalan, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Hungarian, Italian, Norwegian, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish and Ukrainian
api_h2: What the API can — and cannot — do
api_lead: Škoda's public API returns one live reading per request and a short command list. It has no history, which shapes everything Mate does: history is derived by Mate and clearly labelled where it is an estimate. Nothing is ever shown as a number when it is a guess.
c10_p: A card that flags open trips, unseen charge ends and near-duplicates, offers safe fixes with undo, and never shows a guess as a number
c11_p: MQTT discovery with about 40 entities per car: sensors, tracker, buttons and a charge-limit slider (opt-in). Set up in the dashboard, no restart.
c12_p: Signed webhooks for trips, charges, places and battery events, a JSON API with a bearer token, CSV export and database backup
c1_p: Car render, battery, range, charging state, doors/windows/lock, climate, position, last trip and charge, 48 h chart
c2_p: Derived trips with day and month views, search, map, notes, cost, CSV export — plus duplicate-safe import of the MyŠkoda app's trip CSV
c3_p: Sessions with energy, AC/DC, Home/Public, charging curve and cost, with CSV export
c4_p: Your kWh prices for home, public AC and public DC. Costs recalculate everywhere; a charge's real total overrides the estimate
c5_p: SoC history, charging settings and profiles, a capacity estimate built from your charges, and projected range at 100 %
c6_p: Charging on/off, charge limit and mode, charging profiles, climate, auxiliary heater and ventilation — only what this car supports, with a reason when it doesn't
c7_p: Monthly distance, energy, cost and consumption. Charging and Driving tabs with power, charge curves, destinations and heatmaps; a Parked tab for the battery lost while parked
c8_p: Where the car stood and charged, plus named places with radius, colour and per-place prices — visits, days, parked time and cost per place
c9_p: A day timeline of drive, charge, climate and parked time, and an event list with every command you sent
col_approx_n: No history in the API — Mate builds it
col_no_n: The API offers nothing for it — so Mate doesn't pretend
f_inspired: Inspired by leapmotor-mate by Silvio Bressani — independent projects, no shared code.
f_personal: Personal use only: Škoda licenses the public API for private use, not for commercial services. Not affiliated with Škoda Auto.
feat_lead: Every dashboard page, in one glance. Everything runs on your own machine — the only external calls go to Škoda's API and, for maps, OpenStreetMap.
hero_sub: Built on Škoda's official public API with an API key from the MyŠkoda app — no Škoda account password involved. Trips and charges are derived by Mate itself and kept in a local SQLite database. Docker image, one command, no cloud.
hero_tagline: Self-hosted trip tracking and charge logging for Škoda cars, with charging and climate control.
n3: A route line while driving (no position is reported)
n4: Outside temperature, service and warning lights
n5: Battery health (an estimate is shown instead)
n6: Sending a destination to the car
notes: Other ways in: on Unraid the app installs from Community Applications (search skoda-mate), or from the template and compose file in the repo. Any other NAS that runs Docker — Synology, Ugreen, QNAP and others — can use the same docker-compose.yml or the image from Docker Hub. DEMO=1 starts a fictional Enyaq with 60 days of history if you want to look around first; and before a login exists, the setup form asks for a one-time code from the log when reached from a public address
quota: Request budget: Škoda allows about 20 requests per hour per car. Mate polls every 20 minutes while parked and every 5 minutes while charging, climatising or driving, keeps 4 requests reserved for commands, and shows a live counter in the top bar — so you always know what the quota is doing.
s1_p: No image build, nothing to configure first: the image is published on Docker Hub as steffenr/skoda-mate for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
s2_p: Open go.skoda.eu/api-keys, create a key and select all your cars. Paste the key and your VIN(s) in the next step. No Škoda password is ever entered here; the 4-digit S-PIN is optional and only needed to start the auxiliary heater.
s2_t: Create an API key in the MyŠkoda app
s3_p: Go to http://localhost:8080, create your dashboard login and paste the API key. Mate tests it against Škoda and stores it encrypted.
s3_small: Port is yours to change: edit ports in docker-compose.yml. Updates are docker compose pull && docker compose up -d; your ./data folder survives.
s3_t: Open the dashboard and finish setup
setup_lead: Docker is the recommended way; three steps and you are looking at your car
shots_lead: All from the built-in demo: a fictional Enyaq with 60 days of history, no account, no network
sup_lead: Škoda Mate is a spare-time project and stays free software. If it is useful to you, a coffee is appreciated — issues and pull requests on GitHub just as much.
y1: Battery level, range, charging state and power
y4: Start/stop charging, charge limit and mode
